cards.headline:
Underdog's 32MB Woof model
makes speech and music offline
cards.body: Underdog released Woof, an open 31M-parameter speech and music model that runs offline on most devices in just 32MB.

blocks.x: AI companies are racing to build bigger models that need massive processing power, while some researchers and startups are making smaller models that run on edge devices like your phone or computer.

One such startup, Underdog, has released a game built with its new voice model called Woof that's only 32MB large. The game features a room with a retro tech theme, a typewriter, and a CRT monitor; its intro warns users about “intrusive” cloud providers in the town — ostensibly a jab at cloud-based models.

You can type anything on the typewriter and the game will speak it back, or rotate the tuner to generate different kinds of music. All of this works within the browser through Underdog's speech generation model, which, the company says, can run on most devices without any internet connection. The model has 31 million parameters and is open for everyone to download.

The demo comes weeks after Underdog launched Bark, a 167MB speech-to-text model for transcription and dictation on edge devices. Founder Sigil Wen told TechCrunch: “We just want to train the best open models that are American-made, that are open, that are capable and allow people to have private AI.”
Underdog has also released a 27-billion-parameter model that can run on laptops, along with a waitlisted app positioned as a locally hosted alternative to Muse and Instinct.
